verdictScope: 5ee9dec as an executable reference runtime. Not V1 authority, not a clinical or sporting validation.
verdictBasis: Both BLOCKING findings of QRE-V1CP-IMPL are closed (01, 02), and the regression evidence is clean: suite 1080/1080; the differential claim is confirmed; 13,699 fuzz steps with 0 exceptions, 0 caught TypeErrors, 0 non-determinism and 0 JSON round-trip changes. But four claims of the cycle do not hold, and the cycle introduced one regression. (1) SSCTR-V1CPI-03 (I-15) is unchanged on the SSCTR's own scenario: a single declared break after a REST window still reads SHORT and resumes the last completed doses after 21 days without training (QRE-V1CPR-01). (2) A regression introduced by the cycle on every S6 restart with an adverse report: readableF08 drops every S6 check row, so the answered check is asked again before every later decision (QRE-V1CPR-02). (3) The restart's record hold still fails open when the intake's athlete id or date does not match the record (QRE-V1CPR-03). (4) D49 per executed week breaks after a missed ladder or d49 week (QRE-V1CPR-04). (5) C-2 'the return never crosses a race' fails on three routes (QRE-V1CPR-05). (6) Test adequacy: M12 survives, contrary to the cycle's claim; M29 is now determinable and survives; 4 of 24 mutants on the cycle's own code survive, including N14, which restores the exact AF-01 defect (QRE-V1CPR-06). The single bounded cycle is spent, so these close as explicit blockers routed to the next mission, not as another fix loop.

claimCheck.claim: The 13 new full-result differences (H05 s2/s3/s5, H18 s1-s3, H19 s1-s3, H24 s1-s4) are only CLINICAL_HOLD record rows.
claimCheck.evidence: (a) Path-level deep diff with the candidate's CLINICAL_HOLD rows removed from actualLedger: the only remaining differing paths are /inputHash and /trace/reviewHash on the 7 steps whose input record already carries a hold row (H05 s3, s5; H18 s2, s3; H19 s2, s3; H24 s3), and nothing on the other 6. Both fields are digests of the review input, which includes the carried record. Status, action, proposal and reason are unchanged on all 13. (b) Variant run: the harness's carry hook removes CLINICAL_HOLD rows from the carried record before each candidate step. Result: 116/130 steps byte-identical to FREEZE-6. The 14 that differ are the 13 Block 1 steps and H05 s5, which differs only in inputHash and trace.reviewHash, carried over from s4 (A2), as QRE-V1CP-IMPL recorded. None of the 13 record-only steps differs once the rows are removed. (c) The hold rows: one per non-standing CLINICAL step, carrying eventId, eventKind and declaredAt and no reason text (H24 gains a second after its QUALIFIED_CLEARANCE step).

findings.evidence: BACK_PREV, BACK_NEXT and IDIOM_POSSESSIVES are exactly Q01(c) (back from, came/got/went/flew/drove back, back home, back to, be back; on my/our/his/her feet), plus PT 'em pe' and ES 'de pie' as C-Q01-2 permits. Probe of 35 texts, category WORK, base vs candidate: 11 change, all from ASK to NONCLINICAL, and each rests on an approved collocation. Every impact or care text of the failure scenario stays ASK ('banged my head into the door frame', 'back at the clinic again', 'was back in the er', 'back in a brace', 'back in bed', 'head over the handlebars'), as do 'back on Wednesday', 'been back at work', 'by hand' and 'on the other hand'. Clinical texts stay CLINICAL. R7D-H20 s1-s2 now ask interruption.clinicalReason, the approved Q01 question. Negative directed tests exist (QRE-V1CP-01, A1-1), and N23 (re-widening BACK_NEXT) is caught by both.

Both original failure scenarios now hold. A (fever hold, then a readiness restart): weeks 3-5 run 15/15/20, 15/15/20, 25/25/35 in RETURN mode, the week-2 review asks nothing of Situation 1, and S1 window-end answers sent with improved:true anyway give KEEP with no S1 ladder. mutationMethod.base: A pristine sandbox outside the repository: src/, the six v1cp test files and their fixture module, the three policy/catalog JSONs and three review JSONs the runtime reads (found by tracing fs reads), and the R7-D harness lib with the final2 holdout. 104 files, all byte-identical to the worktree. Control run: 65/65 pass.
mutationMethod.perMutant: A fresh copy per mutant (named <id>-<run>), each edit applied only on an exact single occurrence, then node --test on the six v1cp files (65 tests), with V1CP_ROOT unset so the tests resolve to the copy.
mutationMethod.notRun: The legacy suite per mutant: those tests create no F08 markers, facts, restrictions or S6 restarts, so they cannot observe these edits (same rationale as QRE-V1CP-IMPL).
mutationMethod.survivorChecks: Each survivor was run on directed scenarios against the pristine copy and the mutant copy (M12 also with an instrumented copy; M29 with an instrumented copy that records which rows the entryRegions clause decides).

newFindings.title: SSCTR-V1CPI-03 (I-15) is not fixed for a single declared break, and its test is vacuous
newFindings.scenario: The SSCTR's own scenario: hybrid athlete (also with known 5-set rows); weeks 0-3 done; week 4 Mon NEED_REST REST 7 days, no check; week 6 Mon RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE TRAVEL 12-14..12-20. Result: REESTABLISH 'short nonclinical interruption (7 days): resume the last completed doses', class SHORT, no classBySport. Last executed session 2026-12-05. Week 7 runs 40/35/60 with strength at 2x8 RIR 3 (known rows: 4x8 RIR 3). Also a 4-day break straight after a 7-day REST window gives SHORT, 4 days. Identical at fa3985b.
newFindings.cause: The I-15 extension lives in stopOf. returnAfterPause reaches stopOf only through separateStop or recordedStop (separate breaks on record, or a re-read), so a single declared break never reads the window's R0/R1/WAIT days. The directed test uses a 14-day break, already MODERATE, and N11 survives.
newFindings.expected: SSCTR-V1CPI-03: a combination of the two paths is never less conservative than either; per sport, the days the episode kept a sport from training are days of its stop (p5b gives MODERATE).

escalation.why: Sporting dose after 21 days without training.

newFindings.title: Regression introduced by the cycle: readableF08 drops every S6 restart check, so an answered check is asked again before every later decision, and replays duplicate it
newFindings.scenario: Clinical declared break (ILLNESS 'flu'), then a READINESS_DECLARATION, which starts the S6 restart. Thursday: a review reporting Tuesday's run ADVERSE asks wellbeingCheck; answered all no, it gives KEEP and records one WELLBEING_CHECKED (ADVERSE_SESSION), whose episode is the declaration's event id. Friday MISSED_SESSION with no new report: ASK wellbeingCheck 'A session was reported as not going well'. Saturday SCHEDULE_CHANGE: ASK. The following week: ASK. At fa3985b the same steps are KEEP. Separately, replaying a week's WEEKLY_REVIEW with its S6 check (same event id) after adoption appends the RESTART_WEEK row again, 1 then 2 then 3 rows (random fuzz: 34 replays, all RESTART_WEEK).
newFindings.cause: readableF08 keeps a WELLBEING_CHECKED row only when a readable WELLBEING_DECLARED row carries its episode id. S6 checks name the readiness declaration, so they are never read. f08Guard's last check is then null, and its replay guard cannot see the row.
newFindings.expected: C-Q05-4 asks about a session reported after the last check, not about every session again; SEC-V1CPI-10: one event id is one fact; fa3985b behaviour on this path.

escalation.why: The readable-row rule is SEC-V1CPI-04's; which episodes a check may name.

newFindings.title: restartIntake silently drops a CLINICAL_HOLD it cannot read, and returns a new plan over it
newFindings.scenario: Sign-yes entry (W2) on 2026-11-17; the record holds CLINICAL_HOLD (athleteId ath-v1cp-hybrid, declaredAt 2026-11-17T11:00Z). restartProgram({intake, record}) with a TRAVEL pause: with the same id and asOf 2026-11-30, CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED (correct); with intake.athlete.id 'someone-else', PROPOSED; with intake.asOf 2026-11-15 (start 11-16), PROPOSED, while asOf 2026-11-16 still returns CLINICAL. The record's non-F08 history is still read for the pause in every case.
newFindings.cause: restartIntake reads F08 rows through readableF08, with the owner taken from the intake's id and the clock from the intake's day plus 14 hours. Rows it cannot read are skipped, not treated as a mismatch.
newFindings.expected: SEC-V1CP-23 and RC-15: a hold on record blocks a new plan whatever is sent. A record that disagrees with the intake (another athlete's rows, facts after the intake's date) is refused or asked, never read as no hold.

escalation.why: Core boundary decision: fail-closed reading of unreadable holds at a restart.

newFindings.title: D49 per executed week: after a missed ladder or d49 week, strength rises two sets over the last executed week
newFindings.scenario: Known rows 6x8 at 20 kg, RIR 2; NEED_REST REDUCE_SUBSTANTIAL 3 days from week 1 Mon, answered improved at week 1 Sun; weekly reviews with checks; one week's strength not done. BALANCED with the R3 week missed: planned 1 > 2 (missed) > 3, executed 1 > 3. R4 week missed: executed 1 > 2 > 4. FASTER with the d49 week missed: executed 2 > 3 > 5; second d49 week missed: 2 > 3 > 4 > 6. At fa3985b the same scenarios stay within one set, because the held doses were re-established; the cycle's SSCTR-V1CPI-02 fix keeps them, which makes this reachable.
newFindings.cause: ladderCap and d49Hold compare with the previous planned week. The repeated step (I-02, I-04, SSCTR-V1CPI-04) is capped at the missed week's planned sets plus one.
newFindings.expected: returnLadder.transitionRule (D49): at most one set per executed week whatever the rung; C-Q06-3 across the return.

escalation.why: Confirm the per-executed-week reading after a missed rung.

newFindings.title: C-2 'the return never crosses a race' is checked only when the window opens and at the window-end check
newFindings.scenario: (a) MILD_ILLNESS REDUCE_SUBSTANTIAL 5 days from week 1 Tue, answered improved; ladder R2 in week 2, R3 in week 3, R4 in week 4. An EVENT_DATE_CHANGE on week 2 Wed moves the 10K to 2026-12-05, the Saturday of the R3 week: MODIFY REPLAN_FUTURE_PHASES, the race live at race effort beside EASY 20/20, no question (present at fa3985b). (b) EVENT_DATE_CHANGE into an open window: fuzz seeds 203 (R1), 1233 (R0), 1260 (R1). (c) A ladder shifted onto a race: seed 1022. The window-end check on 11-29 gives a ladder ending 12-27 with the race on 12-28, so no ASK. A missed week, then a week with no review of its own (SSCTR-V1CPI-04, new in this cycle), shift the ladder until the race week is R3, with the race kept.
newFindings.cause: raceInReturn runs only in wellbeingCheck and episodeWeekly at the window end, and openWindow asks only at the report. goalChange and the step repeats never re-check the ladder against the race.
newFindings.expected: C-2 (consolidation of SSCTR-V1CPI-05) and C-Q05-3: no race-effort session inside R0-R3, and the race is asked, never only kept.

escalation.why: Rule for a race date change during a window or ladder, and for a ladder that shifts onto a race.

newFindings.title: Test adequacy of the fix cycle: 6 non-equivalent survivors, including the restored BLOCKING defect
newFindings.evidence: M12 survives; the fix cycle says it is killed, but its test sits on the path where the guard is now redundant, and the readiness-path guard is untested. M29 (now determinable) survives. N11 survives (vacuous I-15 test), as do N14 (AF-01 restored, undetected by the QRE-V1CP-02 test), N18 (named-hold check) and N19 (screen-after-hold check). 20 of 24 mutants on the cycle's own code are caught.
newFindings.expected: QRE-V1CP-C2 and C4: each fix has a test that fails when the fix is removed.

newFindings.title: The named-hold check matches undefined to undefined, so a one-key or empty reference to nothing on record is accepted
newFindings.scenario: Continuation hold (S1 sign yes): hold {eventId:'not-on-record'} gives READINESS_RESTART, and so does hold {}. Episode hold (clinical declared break): {eventId:'not-on-record'}, {episodeId:'not-on-record'} and {} all give REESTABLISH. The two-key mismatch is asked (fixed).
newFindings.cause: readReadiness accepts either key alone or none. readinessRestart tests h.eventId===hold.eventId||h.identity===hold.episodeId; continuation holds carry no identity and episode holds no eventId, so an omitted key compares undefined with undefined. Not a hold bypass: the declaration still binds this athlete's own holds.

newFindings.title: A CLINICAL_HOLD on record cannot be released once the reference state is gone, so a new plan is blocked for good
newFindings.scenario: Sign-yes entry, then the reference state is no longer sent (the R7-D harness models a qualified clearance this way; H18, H19 and H24 leave such rows). The weekly review gives KEEP. READINESS_DECLARATION gives KEEP 'No clinical hold, held sport or restriction is on record: there is nothing to restart' and records no READINESS_DECLARED. restartProgram then returns CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED with missingInputs ['readiness'], which can never be satisfied.
newFindings.cause: readinessRestart takes holds from the reference state and kept clinical episodes only; the CLINICAL_HOLD row is used only for screen timing. It fails closed, but leaves no way back to a new plan (DR-148, B6).

escalation.why: Whether the record's hold is also the in-program hold (RC-15) and how a qualified clearance is recorded.

newFindings.title: The race rule also holds a strength-only return: strength waits until a running race is moved, skipped or past
newFindings.scenario: MINOR_DISCOMFORT, STRENGTH only, REST 3 days in week 4 (whole body or LOWER_BODY), with a 10K on 2026-12-19. The window-end check asks to move or skip the race, and strength keeps waiting (fuzz seed 1220: four weeks, until the race passed). It fails closed but is over-broad.

escalation.why: Scope of C-2 when running is not affected.

newFindings.title: The chained 14-day bound can ask 'choose at most 0 days', a question with no valid answer
newFindings.scenario: NEED_REST REST 10 days from week 1 Mon, no check answered; week 3 Tue a new report (UNUSUAL_FATIGUE REST 3 days) gives ASK wellbeing.days 'choose at most 0 days'. One day is refused as out of the options. Seen 18 times in 400 structured seeds. Exits remain: the window-end check offers a declared break or a new plan.

escalation.why: Whether 14 or more continuous days route to the assessment path instead of a days question (RC-06).

regressionProbes.crashesDeterminismReplay: 0 exceptions, 0 caught TypeErrors and 0 non-determinism in 13,699 steps. JSON round trip of the record and reference state never changed a decision. Situation 1 replays are clean (1,380 in the structured profile); S6 replays duplicate the check (QRE-V1CPR-02). Plan-changing UNAVAILABLE_DAY and gated weekly replays are FREEZE-6 behaviour.
regressionProbes.clinicalHoldPath: One hold row on every non-standing CLINICAL result, none on standing or replayed ones. The early clinical finish (a current eligibility flag) now returns the carried record plus the hold row, where FREEZE-6 returned no record: correct for a conforming client. Residues: QRE-V1CPR-03 and -08.
regressionProbes.restartFacts: pause.readinessDeclared, pause.bySportDays and restart in intake data are input errors; a Symbol has no JSON form. A stated cause is screened, and a stated pause never shortens the record's (N16, N17 caught). Programs made by restartProgram validate and review normally. The default path is unaffected (H2 300/300 and generations 39/39 byte-identical).
regressionProbes.readableF08: No legitimate row is lost to a JSON round trip, and owner/clock/seal/shape rejections are as designed (N04 caught). It does drop every S6 check (QRE-V1CPR-02), and drops holds the restart intake cannot read (QRE-V1CPR-03).
regressionProbes.d49HoldTermination: Terminates: markers stop at the held count with 5, 6 and 8 held sets, FASTER, BALANCED and REST; the longest run in the fuzz is 3. The per-executed-week reading fails after a missed week (QRE-V1CPR-04).
